title: Why Do Wombats Poop CUBES? 🟫
description:
Wombats really do poop cubes, up to a hundred a day. And no, a wombat's bottom isn't square: a CT scan of a live wombat showed it's round, like everyone else's. The corners are made inside, in the last part of the gut. Its wall has two stiff stripes, about four times stiffer than the rest, and every squeeze the stiff parts pull in faster than the soft parts, so the drying poop slowly gets four corners (Yang et al., Soft Matter, 2021). Why bother? Wombats leave their poop on rocks and logs, like smelly notes for other wombats, and scientists think a cube is less likely to roll off. Would you have eaten it? Yes or no?

The scientists who worked this out won the 2019 Ig Nobel Prize in Physics.
